request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change to a sheet now writes one line to the audit file, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass. This was a server-only change; the front end didn't need anything.

**What I changed**
- **`Audit.java`**: added `change(event, sheetId, user, fields...)`, which builds the line as `EVENT sheet=<id> by=<user> field=value …`. Inside a transaction the line is written only after the transaction commits, so a refused or rolled-back change writes nothing — including refusals from rules added later.
- **`PersonService` / `ClaimService`**: record `PERSON_ADDED`, `PERSON_EDITED`, `CLAIM_ADDED` and `CLAIM_EDITED`. They save to the database before recording, so database-level failures show up first. The line uses the stored values: the trimmed name, the amount with two decimals, and the date as yyyy-mm-dd (filled with the sheet's today when left blank).
- **`PersonController` / `ClaimController`**: pass the signed-in user from the `X-User` header through to the services.

**Behaviour to be aware of**
- A claim line names the person as they are called when the claim is added or edited. If someone is renamed, older claim lines keep the old name and later edits use the new one.
- Concurrent changes are logged in the order they commit.
